description: Manually labeled validation cases for the claim verifier / external judge. Each case fixes a claim, a small passage pool, and the verdict a correct judge must reach. Labels were authored by hand from the passage text alone; case 5 exists to pin the rule that ABSENCE FROM THE POOL IS NOT FALSITY: a true claim the pool does not cover must land in not_enough_evidence, never contradicted. v1.2.0 keeps the 11 v1.1.0 cases verbatim and adds 10 development cases: the three failure modes measured under verification-v1 (compound partial support, hedged agreement read as contradiction, in-range value read as contradiction), the previously uncovered unsupported verdict, unit/date/entity mismatches, causal-vs-correlational wording, and conflicting-is-not-insufficient. This is a DEVELOPMENT set used to tune the verification prompt; the frozen final test set is never used for tuning. A case may carry acceptable_verdicts (always containing expected_verdict): any verdict in it counts as agreement, used where several verdicts are defensible but one (named in label_basis) is pinned as wrong.

cases.claim: The trial reported a 12% reduction in hospital admissions in the treatment group.

passages.title: Trial results summary
passages.text: In the randomized trial, the treatment group showed a 12% reduction in hospital admissions compared with placebo over 24 months, a statistically significant difference.

passages.title: Unrelated methods note
passages.text: Participants were recruited from twelve outpatient clinics and followed quarterly.

cases.label_basis: Passage 1 states the claim's exact figure and direction verbatim.

cases.claim: The intervention reduced hospital admissions by 12% in all age groups.

passages.title: Trial results summary
passages.text: The treatment group showed a 12% reduction in hospital admissions overall; in participants over 70, however, the reduction was not statistically significant.

passages.title: Recruitment note
passages.text: Participants were recruited from twelve outpatient clinics.

cases.label_basis: The overall 12% figure is supported; the 'all age groups' clause is explicitly not established for the over-70 subgroup.

cases.claim: The study found that the supplement improved marathon finishing times.

passages.title: Supplement trial
passages.text: Marathon finishing times did not improve with supplementation; the supplement group was on average 40 seconds slower than placebo, a non-significant difference in the opposite direction.

passages.title: Adherence note
passages.text: Adherence to the supplementation protocol exceeded 90% in both groups.

cases.label_basis: Passage 1 states the opposite of the claim: no improvement, direction reversed.

cases.claim: Daily meditation lowers systolic blood pressure by at least 8 mmHg in hypertensive adults.

passages.title: Meditation overview
passages.text: Meditation practices have grown in popularity and are studied for a range of stress-related outcomes. Programs vary widely in duration and technique.

passages.title: Hypertension background
passages.text: Hypertension affects roughly one in three adults and is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease.

cases.label_basis: Both passages are topical but neither states anything about meditation's effect size on blood pressure.

cases.claim: Water boils at approximately 100 degrees Celsius at sea-level atmospheric pressure.

passages.title: Espresso extraction
passages.text: Espresso machines extract coffee at around nine bars of pressure, with brew temperatures typically between 90 and 96 degrees Celsius.

passages.title: Kettle market report
passages.text: Electric kettle sales grew steadily, with consumers favouring models with temperature presets.

cases.label_basis: The claim is true in the world, but no passage in the pool states it. Absence from the pool must yield not_enough_evidence, never contradicted - this case exists to pin that rule.

cases.claim: The vaccine was 95% effective against symptomatic infection in the trial.

passages.title: Trial efficacy report
passages.text: Vaccine efficacy against symptomatic infection was 66% in the primary analysis, with confidence intervals from 57% to 74%.

passages.title: Safety summary
passages.text: No serious safety concerns were identified during the follow-up period.

cases.label_basis: The passage states a materially different efficacy figure (66% vs the claimed 95%) for the same outcome in the same trial framing.

cases.claim: The cohort study followed participants for a median of eight years and recorded dietary intake annually.

passages.title: Cohort methods
passages.text: Participants were followed for a median of eight years. Dietary intake was recorded with a validated food-frequency questionnaire administered annually.

passages.title: Cohort funding note
passages.text: The study was funded by a national research council grant.

cases.label_basis: Both halves of the claim (follow-up duration and annual dietary recording) are stated verbatim in the methods passage.

cases.claim: The medication lowered LDL cholesterol by 30% and eliminated cardiovascular risk.

passages.title: Lipid trial outcomes
passages.text: The medication lowered LDL cholesterol by 30% versus baseline. Cardiovascular events were reduced but not eliminated; residual risk remained substantial in all treatment groups.

cases.label_basis: The 30% LDL reduction is stated exactly; the elimination of cardiovascular risk is explicitly negated ('reduced but not eliminated').

cases.claim: Screen time among teenagers declined steadily between 2015 and 2020.

passages.title: Adolescent media survey
passages.text: Average daily screen time among teenagers rose each year from 2015 to 2020, with the largest single-year increase recorded in 2020.

passages.title: Survey methodology
passages.text: The survey sampled approximately 3,000 adolescents annually using a consistent instrument.

cases.label_basis: The passage states the opposite direction over the same period: rose each year rather than declined steadily.

cases.claim: The retraining programme doubled the employment rate of participants within one year.

passages.title: Programme description
passages.text: The retraining programme offers six-month courses in software testing and logistics, with roughly 400 participants enrolled each cohort.

passages.title: Labour market overview
passages.text: Regional unemployment fell modestly during the study period amid broad economic recovery.

cases.label_basis: Passages describe the programme and the labour market but state no employment outcome for participants; the modest regional decline neither supports nor contradicts a doubling claim.

cases.claim: The human heart has four chambers.

passages.title: Exercise physiology note
passages.text: Regular aerobic exercise improves stroke volume and resting heart rate over time.

passages.title: Hospital staffing report
passages.text: Cardiology departments reported increased outpatient volumes last year.

cases.label_basis: A textbook-true anatomical fact that no passage in the pool states. Absence from the pool must yield not_enough_evidence, never contradicted - second anchor for the absence-is-not-falsity rule.

cases.claim: The trial reported improved sleep quality in the treatment group.

passages.title: Trial outcomes
passages.text: The trial's primary and secondary outcomes were systolic blood pressure and body weight; the treatment group improved significantly on both.

passages.title: Trial design
passages.text: The 12-month randomized trial enrolled 840 adults across four centres.

cases.label_basis: The pool squarely addresses this trial's outcomes yet states nothing about sleep quality and nothing against it. Unsupported is the pinned label; not_enough_evidence is acceptable since the boundary is soft - what is wrong is supported or contradicted.

cases.claim: The 2019 survey measured respondents' trust in television news.

passages.title: Survey instrument
passages.text: The 2019 survey asked 2,400 respondents to rate their trust in newspapers, radio bulletins and online news sources on a five-point scale.

passages.title: Survey funding
passages.text: The survey was funded by a consortium of regional broadcasters.

cases.label_basis: The passage describes exactly what the survey measured, and television is not among the media listed - but it never states television was excluded, so contradicted is wrong. Unsupported pinned; not_enough_evidence acceptable.

cases.claim: Moderate alcohol consumption may increase blood pressure.

passages.title: Alcohol and hypertension review
passages.text: Recent studies indicate that even moderate drinking can potentially lead to elevated blood pressure over time.

passages.title: Consumption statistics
passages.text: Per-capita alcohol consumption has declined slightly over the past decade.

cases.label_basis: A hedged claim ('may increase') matched by a hedged passage stating the same direction ('can potentially lead to elevated'). Agreement in hedged form is support; the verification-v1 judge marked this pattern contradicted in the stage-21 inspection.

cases.claim: Between 30% and 60% of patients reported side effects in the pooled trials.

passages.title: Pooled safety analysis
passages.text: Across the pooled trials, 58% of patients reported at least one side effect.

passages.title: Trial registry note
passages.text: Twelve trials met the inclusion criteria for the pooled analysis.

cases.label_basis: A point value (58%) inside the claimed range (30-60%) agrees with the claim. The verification-v1 judge marked an in-range value contradicted in the stage-21 inspection; this case pins that an in-range value is never a contradiction.

cases.claim: Participants received 500 g of vitamin C daily.

passages.title: Supplementation protocol
passages.text: Participants received 500 mg of vitamin C daily throughout the trial, taken with breakfast.

passages.title: Compliance note
passages.text: Pill counts indicated over 95% compliance with the protocol.

cases.label_basis: Same quantity, same protocol, but the units differ by a factor of one thousand (g vs mg). A unit mismatch on the same measurement is a contradiction, not support.

cases.claim: The emissions policy took effect in 2015.

passages.title: Policy timeline
passages.text: The emissions policy, adopted after lengthy consultation, took effect in January 2019.

passages.title: Consultation summary
passages.text: Public consultation on the policy ran for eight months and drew over 3,000 submissions.

cases.label_basis: The passage states a materially different effective date (January 2019 vs the claimed 2015) for the same policy.

cases.claim: Alphaxin reduced migraine frequency by 40% in the head-to-head trial.

passages.title: Head-to-head trial results
passages.text: In the head-to-head trial, Betazol reduced migraine frequency by 40%, while Alphaxin showed no significant reduction.

passages.title: Trial enrolment
passages.text: The head-to-head trial enrolled 612 patients with chronic migraine.

cases.label_basis: The claimed figure exists in the passage but belongs to a different drug, and the passage explicitly states Alphaxin showed no significant reduction. Pins that a matching number attributed to the wrong entity is not support.

cases.claim: Night-shift work causes metabolic syndrome.

passages.title: Occupational health cohort review
passages.text: Large cohort studies report a consistent association between night-shift work and metabolic syndrome; causality has not been established.

passages.title: Shift prevalence
passages.text: Roughly one in five employees in industrialized countries works shifts that include nights.

cases.label_basis: The passage reports a consistent association, which partially supports the causal claim, and itself states causality is not established - so supported is wrong, and the association makes not_enough_evidence wrong too.

cases.claim: The programme increased vaccination coverage by 15 percentage points and was adopted nationwide.

passages.title: Programme evaluation
passages.text: The programme increased vaccination coverage by 15 percentage points in the pilot districts; a national rollout was proposed but has not been adopted.

cases.label_basis: The coverage figure is stated exactly; the nationwide-adoption conjunct is explicitly negated ('has not been adopted'). Third anchor for compound partial support, the verdict verification-v1 scored 0/2 on.

cases.claim: The supplement improves endurance performance.

passages.title: Trial A results
passages.text: In trial A, the supplement improved time-to-exhaustion by 12% versus placebo.

passages.title: Trial B results
passages.text: Trial B found no improvement in endurance performance with the supplement.

cases.label_basis: One passage supports the claim and the other contradicts it: the evidence CONFLICTS, it is not missing. Any verdict that weighs the two sides is acceptable; not_enough_evidence is the pinned wrong answer - conflicting evidence must never be filed as insufficient.
